subject: linear
title: Adding vectors
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Add corresponding components: 2−4, −1+5, 3+1.

subject: linear
title: A dot product
prompt: What is the dot product of (1, 2, −1) and (3, 0, 4)?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Multiply corresponding components and add: 1×3 + 2×0 + (−1)×4 = −1.

subject: linear
title: Euclidean length
prompt: What is the Euclidean norm of (3, 4)?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The norm is √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5.

subject: linear
title: Perpendicular vectors
prompt: Which vector is perpendicular to (2, 1)?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Their dot product is 2×1 + 1×(−2) = 0.

subject: linear
title: Projection onto an axis
prompt: What is the orthogonal projection of (3, 4) onto the x-axis?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Projection onto the x-axis preserves the x-component and removes the y-component.

subject: linear
title: An orthogonal matrix
prompt: For a real orthogonal matrix Q, which identity holds?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The columns of an orthogonal matrix are orthonormal, so QᵀQ is the identity.

subject: linear
title: Matrix multiplication order
prompt: If A is 2×3 and B is 3×4, what is the size of AB?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The inner dimensions agree; the product has the outer dimensions 2×4.

subject: linear
title: A matrix product entry
prompt: A = [[1, 2], [3, 4]] and B = [[2, 0], [1, 5]]. What is the entry in row 1, column 2 of AB?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Dot row 1 of A with column 2 of B: 1×0 + 2×5 = 10.

subject: linear
title: Transposing a product
prompt: Which identity holds for compatible matrices A and B?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Transposition reverses the order of factors.

subject: linear
title: A two-by-two determinant
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: For a 2×2 matrix, the determinant is ad−bc: 2×4 − 1×3 = 5.

subject: linear
title: Swapping rows
prompt: A square matrix has determinant 7. What is its determinant after swapping two distinct rows?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: One row swap changes the determinant’s sign.

subject: linear
title: A triangular determinant
prompt: An upper triangular 3×3 matrix has diagonal entries 2, −3, 4. What is its determinant?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The determinant of a triangular matrix is the product of its diagonal entries.

subject: linear
title: Solving two equations
prompt: Solve x + y = 5 and x − y = 1. What is x?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Adding the equations gives 2x = 6, so x = 3.

subject: linear
title: An inconsistent system
prompt: What can be said about x + y = 1 and 2x + 2y = 3?

options.text: Every pair (x, y) is a solution

source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Doubling the first equation would give 2x + 2y = 2, contradicting the second equation.

subject: linear
title: A homogeneous solution
prompt: Which vector is always a solution of Ax = 0?

options.text: Only vectors with all entries equal to 1

source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Multiplying any matrix by the zero vector gives the zero vector.

subject: linear
title: A subspace test
prompt: Which subset of ℝ² is a vector subspace?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The line y = 2x passes through zero and is closed under addition and scalar multiplication.

subject: linear
title: Linear dependence
prompt: Are (1, 2) and (2, 4) linearly independent?

options.text: No, the second is twice the first
No, because their dot product is zero

source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: One vector is a scalar multiple of the other, so a nontrivial linear combination is zero.

subject: linear
title: Dimension of a basis
prompt: Every basis of ℝ³ contains how many vectors?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The number of vectors in a basis is the dimension of the space.

subject: linear
title: Rank–nullity
prompt: A 3×5 matrix has rank 3. What is the dimension of its null space?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Rank plus nullity equals the number of columns: nullity = 5 − 3.

subject: linear
title: Dependent rows
prompt: What is the rank of [[1, 2], [2, 4]]?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: There is one nonzero independent row; the second row is twice the first.

subject: linear
title: When an inverse exists
prompt: A square real matrix A is invertible exactly when which condition holds?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: A nonzero determinant is equivalent to full rank and invertibility.

subject: linear
title: Inverting a diagonal matrix
prompt: What is the inverse of diag(2, 4)?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The inverse of an invertible diagonal matrix takes the reciprocal of each diagonal entry.

subject: linear
title: Eigenvalues of a diagonal matrix
prompt: What are the eigenvalues of diag(2, 5)?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The standard basis vectors are eigenvectors; their eigenvalues are the diagonal entries.

subject: linear
title: Checking an eigenvector
prompt: For A = [[2, 1], [0, 3]], which eigenvalue corresponds to v = (1, 1)?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam

subject: linear
title: Trace and eigenvalues
prompt: A real 2×2 matrix has eigenvalues 2 and 7. What is its trace?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The trace equals the sum of eigenvalues counted with algebraic multiplicity.

subject: linear
title: Distinct eigenvalues
prompt: Which statement is guaranteed for a real 3×3 matrix with three distinct real eigenvalues?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are independent, giving a basis of three eigenvectors.

subject: linear
title: A planar rotation
prompt: A counterclockwise rotation by 90° maps (1, 0) to which vector?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: A positive quarter turn takes the positive x-axis to the positive y-axis.

subject: linear
title: The kernel of a projection
prompt: For T(x, y, z) = (x, y), what is ker(T)?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: T sends a vector to zero precisely when its x- and y-components are zero.

subject: linear
title: Fitting a constant
prompt: What constant c minimizes (c−1)² + (c−3)² + (c−5)²?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The least-squares constant is the arithmetic mean, (1+3+5)/3 = 3.

subject: linear
title: A positive quadratic form
prompt: For A = diag(2, 3), which statement holds for every nonzero real vector x?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Writing x = (u, v) gives xᵀAx = 2u² + 3v², which is positive unless both components are zero.
